text.p: The Italian Treasury said on Friday it welcomed a decision by the EU's statistical organisation Eurostat clearing its proposed Eurotax and state railway financing plans.
It said in a statement it would also present revised 1992-96 state accounts "in the next few days."
"The Eurostat decision, which concurs in full with the Italian proposals, completes the process of reclassification of the accounts which Italy has submitted," the statement said.
"In the next few days the Treasury Minister will send to parliament the state accounts statistics, recalculated with the new classification criteria, for the 1992-96 period."

Eurostat said the Euro-tax could be used to reduce Italy's deficit. It estimated that the Euro-tax would represent some 0.19 percent of GDP and said the estimated amount to be collected under the tax was 3.5 trillion lire ($.1 billion).

Regarding the treatment of state guarantees for Italy's railway system, Eurostat ruled that "public enterprises' debt guaranteed by the state should be directly taken into account in the government debt".
The reclassification of such debt was expected to reduce Italy's deficit by 0.2 percent of Gross Domestic Product, Eurostat said. The amount involved was seen at 3.7 trillion lire.
Italy said this week it would pass a mini-budget to ensure that it brought its deficit down to the three percent ratio to GDP required for entry into a single European currency in 1999. ($1=1,666)
